Warns that this Next.js version has breaking API/convention changes vs training data and to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before coding. nodes.label: 1 wallet = 1 user Sybil problem
nodes.rationale: Wallets are cheap to create, breaking the 1-wallet-per-user assumption and enabling Sybil attacks across DAO voting, airdrops, agent registries, reputation, marketplaces, and anti-abuse systems. Motivates Judges instead of centralized identity issuers or KYC data collection.

nodes.label: Judges core idea: developer-facing verification layer
nodes.norm_label: judges core idea: developer-facing verification layer

nodes.label: WebAuthn / Passkey ceremony
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it uses the platform security model users already have instead of a new biometric collection system; credentials are relying-party scoped and user verification happens on-device.

nodes.label: Assurance levels: possession / user_verified / unique
nodes.rationale: Introduced because a passkey does not inherently prove '1 credential = 1 human' (synced vs device-bound passkeys per FIDO); prevents Judges from making an unjustified uniqueness claim.

nodes.label: Monad native P256VERIFY (EIP-7951)
nodes.rationale: Monad activated P256VERIFY in the MONAD_FOUR revision, making P-256 verification a protocol-level primitive rather than application-specific cryptography — the key argument for building on Monad.

nodes.label: MonadP256Adapter.sol
nodes.rationale: Isolates the one Monad-specific file (precompile address 0x0100) so porting to another EIP-7951 chain touches one file. Deployed and tested against live Monad Testnet via eth_call, since Foundry fork tests can't reach custom precompiles.

nodes.label: Mode A: onchain P256 + ZK for privacy layer only
nodes.rationale: Hackathon MVP choice: verify WebAuthn/P256 signature off-chain during the ceremony, use ZK only for the privacy-sensitive credential/commitment/nullifier relationship. Easier to demo reliably, still shows Monad P256VERIFY via MonadP256Adapter, avoids an oversized WebAuthn-in-circuit build.
nodes.norm_label: mode a: onchain p256 + zk for privacy layer only

nodes.label: Mode B: full private WebAuthn-in-circuit proof
nodes.rationale: Moves P-256/WebAuthn verification itself into the ZK circuit. Technically demonstrated by an unaudited proof-of-concept (webauth-circom), but not chosen as the hackathon's only security-critical dependency due to cost and audit risk.
nodes.norm_label: mode b: full private webauthn-in-circuit proof

nodes.label: On-chain WebAuthn verification gas spike (§8.1)
nodes.rationale: Measured via contracts/experiments/WebAuthnOnchainSpike.sol: adding on-chain WebAuthn+P256VERIFY on top of the ZK path costs only ~3.5% more gas (~1,166,000 vs ~1,130,000), so gas is not the reason to skip it. The real cost is privacy — P256VERIFY needs the raw public key in calldata, making the passkey a permanent linkable identifier across domains, defeating the nullifier's unlinkability goal (§7.5). Groth16 verification (ecPairing/ecMul at 5x Ethereum pricing on Monad) dominates cost at ~1.13M gas regardless.

nodes.label: Domain-separated nullifier
nodes.rationale: Prevents duplicate use of the same credential secret within a chosen application domain and avoids one universal cross-app identifier; does not prove a person can't create multiple credentials.

nodes.label: JudgesVerifier.sol
nodes.rationale: policyHash is derived inside the contract from contextHash+wallet (never accepted as a caller-supplied parameter) so a caller can't assert an arbitrary binding. VerificationPolicy struct deliberately not implemented since no policy engine exists yet.

nodes.label: NullifierRegistry.sol
nodes.rationale: usedNullifier[domain][nullifier] mapping; HumanVerified event deliberately omits credential id/public key/secret to avoid leaking the identifier it exists to hide.

nodes.label: JudgesRegistry.sol (deliberately not built)
nodes.rationale: Its apparent job (credential/application/binding records) is served by the Postgres tables in §13 since that data must live off-chain to be queried; nothing deployed in its place.

nodes.label: Third-party site popup handshake (/connect)
nodes.rationale: Passkeys are relying-party scoped so a third-party origin cannot run the ceremony itself; the SDK opens a popup on the Judges origin. Safety relies on structural properties, not just user consent: app ids namespaced under the requesting origin, proof posted with targetOrigin=claimed origin, no allowlist needed (permissionless integration).

nodes.label: POST /api/prove endpoint
nodes.rationale: Takes a live WebAuthn assertion (never a bare credentialId) and consumes the same single-use challenge as auth/verify, so a caller can't request a proof for a credential it doesn't control; returns binding inputs, not the derived policyHash, so the contract remains the sole authority on that value.

nodes.label: Backend stack: Next.js API routes on Vercel + Neon + Upstash
nodes.rationale: No standalone server process; chosen so the whole product fits on Vercel/Neon/Upstash free tiers with zero ops. Consequence: anything awaiting Monad tx confirmation must run client-side because serverless functions have an execution time cap.
nodes.norm_label: backend stack: next.js api routes on vercel + neon + upstash

nodes.label: JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Every credential secret, commitment, and nullifier derives from this secret. Effectively permanent — rotating it invalidates every registered passkey and orphans every on-chain-consumed nullifier.

nodes.label: Monad Trust, Identity & AI Infrastructure track fit
nodes.rationale: Rubric weighting: Founder & Market Readiness 25%, Technical Execution 20%, Design & Craft 20%, Traction 20%, Originality 15%. Traction's single highest-value milestone: an external team integrating Judges.
nodes.norm_label: monad trust, identity & ai infrastructure track fit

nodes.label: Roadmap V1/V2/V3
nodes.rationale: V2 adds ZK credential privacy, policy engine, multiple assurance levels, cross-device support, smart account integration; V3 adds human-uniqueness adapters, reputation credentials, AI-agent authorization, cross-chain verification.

nodes.label: Limitations and Honest Claims (§27)
nodes.rationale: Explicit acknowledgments: WebAuthn proves credential control not government identity; user verification doesn't prove uniqueness; synced != hardware-bound passkeys; trusted setup is single-contributor/local and not production-safe; nullifiers can be griefed (not stolen) without a per-submission nonce; credential secret is server-derived (HMAC of JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET) so the backend can compute any registered credential's nullifiers though it cannot forge assertions; 'unique' assurance is a policy label, not an enforced property; Groth16 costs ~1.13M gas on Monad due to 5x-priced ecPairing/ecMul.

nodes.label: Deployment policy: Testnet-only until DoD passes, Mainnet is Phase 9
nodes.rationale: Prevents repeating the risk of promoting to Mainnet before the testnet product is fully validated end-to-end.
nodes.norm_label: deployment policy: testnet-only until dod passes, mainnet is phase 9

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Repository Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Vercel-only hosting decision: apps/web deployed as one unit (frontend+API routes as Vercel Functions), Neon for Postgres, Upstash for Redis, Docker Compose optional local fallback.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — WebAuthn Foundation
nodes.rationale: Discoverable/resident-key credentials via @simplewebauthn/server; Redis GETDEL makes challenges single-use. Not yet verified end-to-end since it needs a real platform authenticator and provisioned Neon/Upstash.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Wallet Binding
nodes.rationale: Binding statement signed by both wallet (EIP-191 personal_sign) and a fresh WebAuthn ceremony whose challenge is sha256(bindingMessage); DB-enforced one-active-binding-per-domain via partial unique indexes rather than only an application-level check.

nodes.label: Foundry fork-test limitation vs custom precompiles
nodes.rationale: --fork-url replays cached state through revm, which has no built-in knowledge of Monad's P256VERIFY, so a naive fork test always returns false at 0x0100 regardless of validity. Confirmed by cross-checking a direct cast call against the live RPC returning 1. Tests use vm.rpc('eth_call', ...) to hit the real forked RPC instead; alternative is vm.etch a mock at 0x0100 for logic-only tests.
nodes.norm_label: foundry fork-test limitation vs custom precompiles

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Nullifier Layer
nodes.rationale: credentialSecret = HMAC-SHA256(JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET, credentialId||publicKey) reduced to BN254 scalar field, standing in for a true authenticator-derived secret since the WebAuthn private key is non-extractable. Poseidon chosen over keccak/sha256 specifically because it's circuit-friendly for Phase 5's ZK proof.

nodes.label: Unauthenticated consume() griefing vector, closed
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated public consume() would let anyone front-run and burn a nullifier before its rightful owner submits. Fixed via a one-time-settable verifier address restricting consume() to JudgesVerifier.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — ZK Privacy Layer (Mode A scope)
nodes.rationale: Circuit proves only points 4-5 of README §8's 5-point statement (nullifier derivation + commitment match), narrower than the idealized statement; points 1-2 stay as onchain P256 verification, point 3 (policy) has no real engine yet so policyHash is carried opaquely but still enforced by Groth16 soundness.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 — zk privacy layer (mode a scope)

nodes.label: MVP-only single-contributor trusted setup
nodes.rationale: prover/scripts/trusted_setup.sh runs a single-contributor local Powers-of-Tau+Groth16 phase-2 ceremony — not production-safe (that contributor could forge proofs). A first attempt to reuse a public Hermez/zkevm .ptau mirror hit AccessDenied on both known hosts, so generating fresh locally was the pragmatic MVP choice.

nodes.label: Phase 6a — JudgesVerifier.sol gap fill
nodes.rationale: Found while starting Phase 6 that no phase ever listed writing JudgesVerifier.sol itself. Built it combining the exported Groth16Verifier with NullifierRegistry, with two deliberate deviations from README's sketch: proof is ABI-encoded Groth16 calldata, and verify() also takes policyHash and wallet.

nodes.label: .gitignore fix: commit frozen zkey/wasm/verification_key.json
nodes.rationale: JudgesGroth16Verifier.sol's verification key is baked in from the exact frozen zkey, so a fresh clone must reproduce compatible proofs without re-running the trusted setup (which would yield an incompatible key). Ceremony intermediates (.ptau/.r1cs/unfinished zkey) stay gitignored.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — SDK
nodes.rationale: Fixed a dependency bug: packages/sdk wrongly depended on the server-only @judges/webauthn package; swapped for @simplewebauthn/browser. Also bumped apps/web tsconfig target from ES2017 to ES2020 because packages/crypto uses BigInt literals.

nodes.label: Phase 7a — proofs-were-bearer-tokens fix
nodes.rationale: Found while designing a demo vote() call: nothing bound a proof to the wallet or action, so anyone could lift a proof from the mempool and submit it as themselves with freely chosen parameters. Fixed per README §7.2 by deriving policyHash = toField(sha256(contextHash||wallet)) inside the contract rather than accepting it as a parameter.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Testnet Deployment
nodes.rationale: This phase's completion equals the hackathon submission; do not proceed to Phase 9 until §8b is done and demoed.

nodes.label: SKIP_FORK_TESTS=1 opt-out flag
nodes.rationale: forge test failed with a DNS error offline because MonadP256Adapter.t.sol self-forks against live RPC. Deliberately opt-out rather than auto-skip, since a silently-skipped test is worse than one that occasionally fails loudly; CI keeps fork tests enabled since GitHub Actions has egress.

nodes.label: Phase 8c — Third-party integration (popup handshake)
nodes.rationale: Found while mapping the build against judging criteria: no other site could use Judges and the SDK wasn't installable, blocking Traction (20%) and Design & Craft (20%). Fixed via a popup handshake so passkeys (relying-party scoped) still work cross-origin, without opening CORS on /api/prove.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Mainnet Promotion
nodes.rationale: Gated on all Definition of Done items passing on testnet, demo video existing, and an explicit team decision — do not skip straight here.

nodes.label: JudgesField library
nodes.rationale: The one on-chain definition of the field prime, hashToField, and policyHash, mirroring packages/crypto; pinned against it by JudgesField.t.sol to prevent silent drift between the TS and Solidity halves.

nodes.label: Contracts → Monad Testnet deploy runbook
nodes.rationale: DeployJudges.s.sol deploys in dependency order and spends the one-shot setVerifier itself; a second deploy produces a fresh independent registry rather than repointing the old one.

nodes.label: Web app → Vercel deployment
nodes.rationale: RP_ID must exactly match the visited hostname since WebAuthn is origin-scoped; Vercel preview URLs get different hostnames so passkeys don't carry over. JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET must be set once and backed up, never rotated casually.

nodes.label: App-id namespacing under requesting origin
nodes.rationale: Without namespacing, any site could open the popup, get a user to tap their passkey, and spend that user's one-per-app action inside someone else's airdrop or DAO. Namespacing means no allowlist or registration with Judges is needed to integrate.

nodes.label: Trusted setup is MVP-only warning
nodes.rationale: pnpm run setup runs a single-contributor local Powers-of-Tau + Groth16 phase-2 ceremony; not production-safe. Mirrors the same 'MVP-scoped, explicitly flagged' pattern used elsewhere (NullifierRegistry's single-settable verifier, P256 test vector notes).

nodes.label: Circuit public inputs rationale (policyHash/applicationIdHash)
nodes.rationale: policyHash isn't checked against real policy logic yet, but Groth16 soundness binds every public signal into the verification equation, so substituting a different policyHash still fails verification. applicationIdHash is reused for both the commitment's domain separator and the nullifier's application id, narrowing packages/crypto's more general TS API; witnesses must go through deriveMembershipWitness to guarantee a satisfiable witness.

nodes.label: Aturan wajib (mandatory rules): secrets, env files, domain-secret rotation ban, honest claims
nodes.rationale: Never put private keys/seeds/tokens/secrets in repo/chat/screenshots (deployer key via --keystore/--ledger only); env files gitignored; JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET held by one person, backed up, never rotated (rotation invalidates all passkeys/nullifiers); all passkeys registered before the Task 2 (redesign B) deploy must re-register; claims must stay honest — Judges proves 'passkey holder present', not 'unique human', since registration currently uses attestationType:'none' with no rate limit so one person can hold many passkeys; test fixtures must be script-generated, not hand-copied.

nodes.label: Tugas 1: Deploy current version to testnet
nodes.rationale: Target 18 Sep, first priority. Dry run via DeployJudgesTest, deploy with funded key to chain 10143, verify via Sourcify (explorer verifier env still empty), fund faucet, create DAO proposal, provision Neon+Upstash+migrate, deploy apps/web to Vercel with listed env vars, then manual E2E test (register/bind/prove, double-claim/double-vote revert checks), record addresses in docs/architecture.md.
nodes.norm_label: tugas 1: deploy current version to testnet

nodes.label: Tugas 2: Redesign B — client-side secret generation
nodes.rationale: 6-working-day timebox, target 26 Sep; if missed, stop and submit current version with existing README §27.8 disclosure. Problem: credentialSecret is server-derived (HMAC of JUDGES_DOMAIN_SECRET), so the backend can compute anyone's nullifier and correlate activity. Design B: secret generated client-side (primarily a deterministic wallet signature hashed to field; WebAuthn PRF as an optional upgrade only, since support is uneven and cross-device output-equality is unproven); identityCommitment = Poseidon(secret); server stores only the commitment; server builds a LeanIMT (zk-kit) off-chain and posts the root on-chain with root history so slightly-stale-root proofs remain valid; new circuit does Merkle membership depth 20 + nullifier = Poseidon(secret, applicationIdHash, epoch); wallet/action binding stays as before via public input; new trusted setup (ptau 2^14) and re-exported verifier/fixtures; proving moves to the browser via snarkjs, and /api/prove is removed/unused; public SDK API (register/prove/verify) is preserved so integrators don't change code. Residual limitation to document: the server can still censor or add a leaf; B does not add sybil resistance.
nodes.norm_label: tugas 2: redesign b — client-side secret generation

nodes.label: Redesign B measurements (M1 circuit experiment)
nodes.rationale: Current circuit: 1.2k constraints, ~115ms browser proving, 0.55MB zkey. Membership depth-20 circuit: 11.4k constraints, ~680ms browser proving, 4.9MB zkey. PoseidonT3 (poseidon-solidity 0.0.5) matches circomlib/poseidon-lite. On-chain LeanIMT insert gas on Monad averages ~609k, worst-case ~897k — too expensive, hence off-chain tree construction (full on-chain registration option already rejected). Per-action Groth16 verification on Monad stays ~1.13M gas, not significantly changed by Redesign B. Must additionally measure: real-device proving time (mid-range Android + iPhone — Chrome CPU throttling is invalid since it doesn't slow Web Workers), root-post gas, and whether signature determinism holds for supported wallets (smart wallets/MPC may not).

nodes.label: Tugas 3: Publish SDK to npm
nodes.rationale: Target 20 Sep after Task 1 is live. Check @judges npm scope availability (rename + update docs/integration.md if unavailable); publish 0.x and confirm docs/integration.md examples work from the npm package; after Redesign B, publish a new version without changing the public API.

nodes.label: Tugas 4: Traction — at least one other team integrates
nodes.rationale: Starts immediately, live integration target 4 Okt. Build a 10-15 candidate list (other hackathon teams / Monad projects: faucet, DAO/voting, airdrop, AI agent, game/quest); pitch 'private anti-bot one-action-per-passkey, popup integration'; hand over docs/integration.md and examples/external-dapp; offer pairing calls; collect evidence (repo/PR, live URL, tx hash, testimonial) tracked in one sheet.
